messages:
Priya (PM): FYI — ACME Finance just raised a formal request: they need a console view to reconcile billed tokens with sampled request traces. Key asks: per-tenant + per-route cost slices, CSV export, and ability to jump from a cost row to a sampled request trace that shows model variant, quantization, batch size, KV-cache hit/miss, and per-token latency. They said this is gating their procurement.

Javier (Support): Copy of customer note pasted below. They want to be able to answer: 'Which requests caused spikes in cost last month and what model/config was used?' They flagged a handful of slow requests and shared logs.

insights-bot: Uploaded files: acme_sample_traces_2026-03-12.log (link) :file_folder:

Lena (Sales): ACME is willing to sign a 12mo Dedicated contract if we can provide a reliable audit view. Main condition: token content must be redacted in export for PII compliance. They still need token-level latency numbers and the model metadata.

Aiden (Eng): Quick tech check — we currently log: model, model_version, route, latency_ms_total, tokens_in, tokens_out, batch_size, kv_cache_hit_ratio. We don't record per-token latency by default. We can sample requests and run a per-token timer in the runtime but it adds ~5-15% overhead for sampled invocations. Thoughts on sampling rate?

Sana (SRE): For production safety, we should limit sampling to 0.1%-1% for hosted customers. For Dedicated we can configure higher. Also need opt-in on Private deployments. We'll need a toggle in Serving runtime + telemetry pipeline to tag sampled traces.

Priya (PM): Proposed scope (MVP): 1) Instrumentation: sampled per-request token-latency + metadata (no token text), 2) Backend: new trace store and queryable index keyed by tenant+route+time, 3) UI: console panel showing cost slices with a drilldown modal that lists sampled traces and CPU/GPU annotation, 4) Export: redacted CSV for finance. Acceptance criteria: sample trace exists for >95% of spike windows in test dataset; export contains model/quantization/batch and per-token latency but no token text.

Javier (Support): Customer provided example of what they want in CSV:
```
timestamp,tenant,route,model,quantization,batch_size,tokens_in,tokens_out,total_latency_ms,token_latencies_ms
2026-03-11T14:12:03Z,acme,/generate,redwood-13b,q4_0,8,32,78,1200,"[10,11,9,12,...]"
```
They asked for a sampled array for token_latencies_ms (numbers only).

Aiden (Eng): We should avoid storing long arrays in main index; instead store a small summary in index (p50/p90/p99, hist buckets) and full sampled payload in object storage with a pointer. Query UI can fetch sample on demand. That keeps DB costs down.

Sana (SRE): Agree. Also add retention policy: summarized data 13 months, raw sampled traces 90 days by default. Dedicated customers can extend. Need to update privacy docs for redaction.

Priya (PM): Prioritization asks: ACME is Enterprise ARR >= threshold. Recommend we treat as sales-assisted priority P1 for Dedicated sales bucket. Proposed timeline: Discovery + infra spike (2w), runtime sampling PoC (2w), backend store + query API (3w), console UI + export (3w), internal rollout + docs (2w) = ~12w. Contingency: split into two releases — infra + sampling + minimal API (release 1) and full UX/export (release 2).

Lena (Sales): If we split, ACME wants release 1 to include the drill-to-sample UX even if CSV export comes later. They care about being able to justify the spend during procurement.

Priya (PM): OK adjust plan: release 1 = sampling + backend + lightweight modal to view a single sampled trace; release 2 = bulk CSV export and advanced filtering.

Aiden (Eng): Risks: sampling adds perf overhead. Need benchmark targets: <=5% p95 latency regression on non-sampled requests. Also need to ensure telemetry pipeline scales for 1M requests/day customers.

Sana (SRE): Notes for rollout: feature flag per-tenant, quota on sampled traces per-day, alerting on ingestion lag >30s.

Priya (PM): Next steps: 1) Aiden + Sana to do infra spike and cost estimate by EOD Friday, 2) Javier to confirm exact redaction rules from ACME legal, 3) I'll write an RFC with acceptance criteria and rollout plan. If SD decides, we'll create an epic and move to backlog.

Javier (Support): I've asked ACME legal for the acceptable redaction template. They replied they only need token text removed and a hash of the token sequence for deduping.

Lena (Sales): :thumbsup: workable. Please flag any blockers — customer wants us to start asap.

Aiden (Eng): I'll start the PoC for per-token timers on a branch and share perf microbenchmarks.

Priya (PM): Thanks everyone. I'll open the RFC and link it here when ready. :eyes:
